title: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Overview
text:
Antyodaya Anna Yojana gives the poorest of the poor households a fixed 35 kg of foodgrains per family every month, and under PMGKAY this grain is free of cost. States pick the families (such as landless labourers, destitute people, primitive tribal households, and widows, disabled or elderly people without support) and give them an AAY ration card. The scheme is active and is part of the National Food Security Act.
Central government scheme. Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

title: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
text:
- Meant for the poorest of the poor households, identified by the State/UT government under the AAY guidelines.
- Landless agricultural labourers, marginal farmers, and rural artisans or craftsmen such as potters, tanners, weavers, blacksmiths and carpenters.
- Slum dwellers, destitute persons, and people earning a daily living in the informal sector, such as porters, coolies, rickshaw pullers, hand-cart pullers, fruit and flower sellers, snake charmers, rag pickers and cobblers, in rural or urban areas.
- Households headed by a widow, a terminally ill or disabled person, or a person aged 60 years or more, with no assured means of living or social support.
- Widows, terminally ill or disabled persons, persons aged 60 years or more, and single women or single men who have no family or social support and no assured income.
- All primitive tribal households.
- Eligible BPL families with an HIV-positive member are to be included on priority.
- Up to 2.5 crore poorest families can be covered across the country, within ceilings fixed for each state.
Not eligible:

title: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
text:
- Only households identified by the state under the AAY guidelines get an AAY card, and a state can add families only within the ceiling the Centre has fixed for it.
- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards are removed when states verify their lists.

title: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Benefits
text:
- Each AAY household gets 35 kg of foodgrains per month, whatever the size of the family.
- Under PMGKAY the grain is given free of cost; free distribution started on 1 January 2023 and has been continued for five years from 1 January 2024.
- Before free distribution, the prices in the Act were Rs 3 per kg for rice, Rs 2 per kg for wheat and Rs 1 per kg for coarse grains.
- Under One Nation One Ration Card, the grain can be taken from any ePoS-enabled ration shop in India.
- If the state does not supply the entitled grain, the household can claim a food security allowance from the state government.

title: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — How to apply
text:
- Approach the Food and Civil Supplies office of your State/UT; states identify AAY families and issue them a distinctive AAY ration card.
- Collect grain from your fair price (ration) shop with the AAY ration card; any household member can collect it.
- For complaints, use your state helpline or the District Grievance Redressal Officer, and appeal to the State Food Commission if needed. The department lists toll-free number 1967 and Anna Sahayata IVRS 14457.

title: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Documents needed
text:
- AAY ration card to collect grain.
- Identity is checked at the ration shop by Aadhaar-based fingerprint or iris scan, or by Aadhaar OTP or PDS OTP.
- If Aadhaar authentication fails, or Aadhaar is missing or not linked, one of 8 alternative identity documents notified on 08.02.2017 can be used; genuine beneficiaries should not be refused grain.
- The documents needed for a new AAY card are decided by your state government.

title: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) — Overview
aliases: आयुष्मान भारत प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना
text:
Free, cashless hospital treatment of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year at empanelled public and private hospitals across India. It covers poor and vulnerable families listed in the scheme's database (SECC 2011 plus later additions), and all people aged 70 or above.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (implemented by the National Health Authority).

title: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) — Eligibility rules
aliases: आयुष्मान भारत प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना
text:
- Eligibility depends on your family being in the scheme's list of eligible families; most families cannot join just by filling a form.
- In rural areas, SECC 2011 families that meet deprivation criteria D1 to D7 (except D6) are covered, for example SC/ST households and families with no adult male member aged 16 to 59.
- In urban areas, SECC 2011 families of workers in 11 listed occupation groups are covered.
- Households automatically included in SECC 2011, such as destitute families living on alms, are covered.
- Families holding an active RSBY card are also covered.
- In January 2022 the list was widened from 10.74 crore to 12 crore families, and many states cover extra families at their own cost.
- Every person aged 70 or above is covered regardless of income, through the Ayushman Vay Vandana card.
- There is no limit on family size, age or gender.
Not eligible:
- Families not in the eligible list cannot get the card simply by applying; only people aged 70 or above can enrol themselves.
- Seniors aged 70 or above who already get free treatment under CGHS, ECHS, CAPF or a state government health scheme must choose only one scheme.

title: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) — Benefits
aliases: आयुष्मान भारत प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना
text:
- Free, cashless treatment of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospital stays and day-care procedures.
- The cover pays for doctor visits, treatment, medicines, consumables, ICU and non-ICU care, implants, a general-ward bed, the patient's food and complications during treatment.
- Tests and medicines for up to 3 days before admission, and medicines for up to 15 days after discharge, are covered.
- Illnesses you already had before joining are covered from the first day.
- You can get treatment at any empanelled hospital in any state (national portability).
- The first PVC Ayushman card is free; reissuing a PVC card costs Rs 15 plus GST.

title: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) — How to apply
aliases: आयुष्मान भारत प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना
text:
- Check whether your family is eligible at beneficiary.nha.gov.in, on the Ayushman app, by calling the helpline 14555, or at a Common Service Centre or empanelled hospital.
- If eligible, complete Aadhaar e-KYC to get your Ayushman card, either yourself on the app or portal, or with help at a CSC or the hospital's Ayushman Mitra desk.
- For treatment, go to an empanelled hospital's Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitra desk with your Ayushman card; no payment is needed for covered care.

title: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) — Documents needed
aliases: आयुष्मान भारत प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना
text:
- Aadhaar: Aadhaar e-KYC is compulsory to make the Ayushman card, except in some emergencies.
- For children up to 5 years, Bal Aadhaar can be used, with a parent's biometric authentication.
- During verification you may be asked for an individual photo ID and a family identity document, such as a ration card.
- At the hospital, show your Ayushman card; if you do not have it, an accepted ID document can be used.

title: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Overview
aliases: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances
text:
ADIP gives people with disabilities durable aids and assistive devices such as wheelchairs, tricycles, artificial limbs, calipers and hearing aids, free or at half cost, depending on income. It is open to Indian citizens of any age with at least 40% disability and a monthly income of Rs 30,000 or less.
Central government scheme. Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

title: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
aliases: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances
text:
- Must be an Indian citizen; there is no age limit.
- Must have a disability of at least 40%, shown by a UDID card (or UDID enrolment number) together with a disability certificate.
- Must give an Aadhaar number or Aadhaar enrolment ID.
- The person's own monthly income from all sources must be Rs 30,000 or less.
- For a dependant (such as a child), the monthly income of the parents or guardians must be Rs 30,000 or less.
- Must not have received help for the same purpose from any source in the last 3 years; for children below 18, custom items like orthosis, prosthesis and learning material can be given again after 1 year.
- For a motorised tricycle or motorised wheelchair: aged 16 years or above with at least 80% disability (severe locomotor disability, stroke, cerebral palsy, hemiplegia or similar), given once in five years.
Not eligible:
- People whose monthly income (or parents'/guardians' income, for dependants) is more than Rs 30,000.
- People who received an aid for the same purpose from any source in the last 3 years.
- People with disability below 40% (except some school children covered under ADIP-SSA through a joint certificate).

title: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
aliases: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances
text: - People aged 16 and above with cognitive impairment cannot get a motorised tricycle or motorised wheelchair, for safety reasons.

title: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Benefits
aliases: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances
text:
- The full cost of the aid or appliance is paid if monthly income is up to Rs 22,500; 50% of the cost is paid if monthly income is Rs 22,501 to Rs 30,000.
- Aids costing up to Rs 15,000 get full assistance; for aids costing Rs 15,001 to Rs 30,000 the assistance is up to Rs 15,000, and any extra can come from CSR, MP/MLA LAD funds, state or local body funds, or the person.
- Motorised tricycle or motorised wheelchair: subsidy of Rs 50,000; high-end prosthesis for locomotor disability of 40% or more: subsidy of Rs 30,000.
- Cochlear implant with surgery and therapy for children with hearing impairment: up to Rs 7 lakh for children aged 1 to 5 with hearing loss from before speech, and up to Rs 6 lakh for children aged 5 to 18 with acquired hearing loss.
- Needed corrective surgery before fitting is also covered: Rs 1,500 for speech and hearing, Rs 3,000 for visual and Rs 15,000 for orthopaedic disability.
- Travel fare of up to Rs 250 each for the person and one escort; for those with monthly income up to Rs 22,500, boarding and lodging of Rs 100 per day (up to 15 days for surgery, 5 days for prosthesis/orthosis or ear mould fitting).

title: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — How to apply
aliases: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances
text:
- Apply online for an assistive device on the ARJUN portal of the Department (adip.depwd.gov.in); eligible requests are to be served within 6 months of registration.
- Attend an assessment and distribution camp held at district level by implementing agencies such as ALIMCO.
- Or visit an ALIMCO centre, National Institute, Composite Regional Centre (CRC) or District Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC) directly.
- Devices are given after assessment, prescription and fitting by an RCI-registered rehabilitation professional.

title: Scheme of Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP Scheme) (ADIP) — Documents needed
aliases: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances
text:
- UDID card or UDID enrolment number, with a disability certificate showing at least 40% disability.
- Aadhaar number or Aadhaar enrolment ID.
- Income proof: income certificate from revenue authorities, BPL card, MGNREGA card, disability pension card, or a certificate from an MP, MLA, councillor or gram pradhan.
- If no income proof is available, a self-declaration or notarised affidavit may be accepted by the implementing agency.
- For people in orphanages, special schools or special homes, an income certificate from the District Collector or head of the institution.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Overview
text:
A financing facility that gives 3% yearly interest subvention for up to 7 years and a government-paid credit guarantee on bank loans of up to Rs 2 crore per project. It is open to farmers, FPOs, PACS, SHGs, agri-entrepreneurs, start-ups and others building post-harvest and community farming infrastructure such as warehouses and cold storage.
Central government scheme. Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
text:
- Individual farmers, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups can apply.
- Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and their federations, Self Help Groups and their federations, and Joint Liability Groups can apply.
- Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), marketing and multipurpose cooperative societies, and national and state federations of cooperatives can apply.
- APMCs, State agencies, and PPP projects sponsored by Central, State or local bodies can apply.
- The loan must be for an eligible post-harvest management project or community farming asset, such as warehouses, cold storage, sorting and grading units, primary processing, or smart and precision farming infrastructure.
- The applicant must put in at least 10% of the fixed project cost as own contribution (margin).
- A private applicant can get benefits for up to 25 projects, each in a different village or town with its own LGD code.
Not eligible:
- Standalone secondary processing units are not eligible.
- Tractors and non-refrigerated transport vehicles cannot be financed for individual farmers.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
text:
- Projects for alcoholic beverages, textile weaving, cosmetic products, bamboo furniture or textiles, and protein powder supplements are listed as ineligible.
- The interest subvention does not apply to the part of a loan above Rs 2 crore per project.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Benefits
text:
- Interest subvention of 3% a year on loans up to Rs 2 crore per project in one location.
- The interest subvention is given for up to 7 years.
- On the subvented loan amount, the lender's interest rate is capped at 9%.
- Credit guarantee cover under CGTMSE for loans up to Rs 2 crore without collateral, with the guarantee fee paid by the Government for up to 7 years.
- Repayment period of up to 7 years, including a moratorium of 6 months to 2 years.
- Can be combined with subsidies from other Central and State schemes (such as PMKSY, PMFME and PM-KUSUM) for eligible projects.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — How to apply
text:
- Register on the AIF portal agriinfra.dac.gov.in using your mobile number and an Aadhaar-based OTP.
- Fill the online application, choose the bank or lending institution, and upload a Detailed Project Report (DPR); DPR templates are on the portal in English and Hindi.
- The Central PMU checks the application and sends it to the chosen lender, which appraises and sanctions the loan, normally within 60 days.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Documents needed
text:
- Bank's loan application form or request letter for an AIF loan, with passport-size photographs.
- Identity proof such as Voter ID, PAN, Aadhaar or driving licence, and address proof.
- Land ownership or lease documents for the project site.
- Detailed Project Report with required permissions, layout plans and building sanctions.
- Bank statements, repayment record of existing loans and, if available, income tax returns and balance sheets for the past three years.
- For firms and organisations, registration proof (such as DIC or Udyam registration, firm or company registration) and GST certificate.

title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) — Overview
text:
A government-guaranteed pension scheme, mainly for unorganised-sector workers. People who join between 18 and 40 pay a small amount regularly and get a fixed pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month from age 60, which then goes to the spouse. Since 1 October 2022, people who pay or have paid income tax cannot join.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services (administered by PFRDA).

title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Must be a citizen of India.
- You can join from age 18 up to your 40th birthday. After your 40th birthday you can no longer join, so in practice the joining age is 18 to 39.
- Must have a savings account in a bank or post office, because contributions are auto-debited from it.
- Must not be an income-tax payer now or in the past. This applies to new accounts opened from 1 October 2022.
- Meant mainly for workers in the unorganised sector, but any eligible citizen can join.
- You keep contributing until age 60, so you contribute for at least 20 years.
Not eligible:
- From 1 October 2022, anyone who is or has been an income-tax payer cannot open a new APY account.
- If someone who joined on or after 1 October 2022 is later found to have been an income-tax payer, there is no penalty, but the account is closed and the money saved so far is returned.
- Each person can have only one APY account.
- People under 18, or past their 40th birthday, cannot join.

title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) — Benefits
text:
- From age 60 you get a guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000, in slabs of Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000. Your pension depends on the slab you choose and what you pay in.
- If investment returns are too low to pay the promised minimum pension, the Central Government covers the gap. If returns are higher, the pension can be higher.
- When the subscriber dies, the spouse gets the same pension for life. When both have died, the nominee gets the pension wealth built up until the subscriber's age 60.
- If the subscriber dies before 60, the spouse has two choices. They can keep paying into the account until the subscriber would have turned 60 and then get the pension, or they can take the whole amount saved.
- The monthly contribution depends on your joining age and pension slab. It is Rs 42 to Rs 210 a month if you join at 18, and Rs 291 to Rs 1,454 a month if you join at 40.
- You can leave the scheme early by choice, but you get back only your own contributions plus the earnings on them, minus account charges.

title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) — How to apply
text:
- Go to the bank branch or post office where you have your savings account and fill in the APY registration form.
- You can also join online through eAPY on the NPS Trust website (npstrust.org.in), or through net banking or the mobile app of some banks.
- Choose to pay monthly, quarterly or half-yearly by auto-debit. If a payment is late, the bank charges Rs 1 for every Rs 100 due, for each month of delay.
- You can raise or lower your pension slab once in each financial year.

title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) — Documents needed
text:
- Details of your bank or post office savings account (mandatory).
- Nominee details (mandatory).
- Aadhaar number (useful but not mandatory when joining).
- Mobile number, to get updates.

title: Ayushman Vay Vandana – AB PM-JAY for Senior Citizens aged 70 years and above (Ayushman Vay Vandana) — Overview
text:
Free hospital treatment cover of up to Rs 5 lakh a year for every person aged 70 or above, whatever their income. It is given through a separate Ayushman Vay Vandana card under AB PM-JAY. Families already in PM-JAY get it as an extra top-up for their members aged 70 or above.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (implemented by the National Health Authority).

title: Ayushman Vay Vandana – AB PM-JAY for Senior Citizens aged 70 years and above (Ayushman Vay Vandana) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Aged 70 years or above.
- There is no income limit: anyone aged 70 or above can join, whatever the family's income or economic status.
- Age is checked only from Aadhaar, and Aadhaar e-KYC is compulsory.
- If Aadhaar shows only the year of birth, the date of birth is taken as 1 January of the next year (for example, birth year 1954 is treated as 1 January 1955).
- Having a private health insurance policy does not stop you from joining.
- Members of the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) scheme can also join.
Not eligible:
- People below 70 years cannot get this card, though they may qualify for regular PM-JAY.
- If you already get free treatment under CGHS, ECHS, CAPF or another central or state government health scheme, you must choose either that scheme or PM-JAY; the choice is one-time and final.

title: Ayushman Vay Vandana – AB PM-JAY for Senior Citizens aged 70 years and above (Ayushman Vay Vandana) — Benefits
text:
- Free hospital treatment cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per year, shared by all members of the family aged 70 or above.
- If the family is already in PM-JAY, its members aged 70 or above get an extra top-up of up to Rs 5 lakh a year on top of the family's existing cover.
- In a family that is new to PM-JAY, the cover is only for members aged 70 or above, not for younger members.
- Each eligible senior gets a separate Ayushman card, even if the family already has PM-JAY cards.
- Treatment is cashless at PM-JAY empanelled hospitals across India, with the same benefits as regular PM-JAY.

title: Ayushman Vay Vandana – AB PM-JAY for Senior Citizens aged 70 years and above (Ayushman Vay Vandana) — How to apply
text:
- Apply yourself on the Ayushman app or at beneficiary.nha.gov.in, using Aadhaar e-KYC by OTP, fingerprint or iris scan.
- A registration operator (such as an ASHA worker or another authorised operator) can also do the enrolment for you.
- Enrolment is open throughout the year.
- Use the 'add member' option to enrol your spouse or another family member who is also 70 or above.

title: Ayushman Vay Vandana – AB PM-JAY for Senior Citizens aged 70 years and above (Ayushman Vay Vandana) — Documents needed
text:
- Aadhaar card is the only document needed; Aadhaar e-KYC is compulsory.
- A live photo is taken during enrolment and printed on the card.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Overview
aliases: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) - old scheme it replaced
text:
DAY-NRLM brings at least one member of each poor rural household, preferably a woman, into a Self Help Group (SHG). It then supports these groups with a Revolving Fund of Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, community investment funds, bank loans without collateral, interest subvention and training. The mission is ongoing and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development through State Rural Livelihoods Missions.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
aliases: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) - old scheme it replaced
text:
- Meant for rural poor households: at least one member of each identified poor household, preferably a woman, is brought into a Self Help Group.
- Poor households are identified by the community through the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process, and the list is vetted by the Gram Sabha; the BPL list alone is not used.
- SHGs usually have 10 to 20 members, mostly women; special SHGs in remote tribal or difficult areas, or of vulnerable people such as persons with disabilities, may have as few as 5 members.
- Groups of persons with disabilities, elderly people or transgender persons may include both men and women; other SHGs are women's groups.
- To get the Revolving Fund, an SHG should have existed for at least 3 to 6 months, follow the Panchasutras and not have received a Revolving Fund before.
- To get a bank loan, an SHG must have been active for at least 6 months as per its books of account and follow the Panchasutras: regular meetings, regular savings, regular inter-loaning, timely repayment and up-to-date books.
- The SHG must qualify under the grading norms fixed by NABARD.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
aliases: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) - old scheme it replaced
text:
- The poorest, single women, women-headed households, persons with disabilities, landless people and migrant labourers get special focus.
Not eligible:
- The mission is for rural areas; the interest subvention is only for women SHGs in rural areas.
- An SHG that has already received a Revolving Fund earlier cannot get it again.
- Interest subvention is given only while the SHG loan account stays in the standard (regularly repaid) category.
- A defunct SHG can get credit only after it is revived and stays active for at least 3 months.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Benefits
aliases: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) - old scheme it replaced
text:
- Revolving Fund of Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 per SHG to build its funds and credit history.
- Community Investment Fund (CIF) given through village and cluster federations, which lend it to SHGs or use it for joint activities.
- No collateral is needed for SHG bank loans up to Rs 20 lakh, and no margin is taken for loans up to Rs 10 lakh.
- Term loan doses: first dose at least Rs 1.5 lakh (or 6 times the group's corpus), second dose at least Rs 3 lakh (or 8 times the corpus), third dose at least Rs 6 lakh.
- Women SHGs in rural areas get bank loans up to Rs 3 lakh at a concessional interest rate of 7% per year (terms for 2025-26).
- Training and capacity building for members, plus self-employment training through Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) and help to access insurance.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — How to apply
aliases: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) - old scheme it replaced
text:
- Contact the State Rural Livelihoods Mission staff at your block office (Block Mission Management Unit) or the SHG / Village Organisation in your village to join or form an SHG.
- Existing SHGs can also be brought under the mission; groups that meet its norms become eligible for the Revolving Fund, CIF and interest subvention.
- myScheme lists an online registration on the Aajeevika portal (aajeevika.gov.in/en/member/register) using name, email and mobile number and creating a username and password.
- Once the SHG meets the conditions, it applies for a loan at a bank branch.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Documents needed
aliases: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) - old scheme it replaced
text:
- Aadhaar number
- Proof of identity
- Proof of residence
- Voter ID card
- Passport size photograph

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — Overview
aliases: दीन दयाल उपाध्याय ग्रामीण कौशल्य योजना
text:
Free job-skill training linked to a job placement, for young people from poor rural families aged 15 to 35 (up to 45 for women and some special groups). Since 2025-26 the scheme runs under revised 'DDU-GKY 2.0' rules, so some amounts may have changed.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — Eligibility rules
aliases: दीन दयाल उपाध्याय ग्रामीण कौशल्य योजना
text:
- Must be a young person from a poor family living in a rural area.
- Aged 15 to 35 years.
- The upper age limit is 45 years for women, Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), persons with disabilities, transgender persons and other special groups such as rescued bonded labourers, trafficking victims, manual scavengers and people living with HIV.
- The household's poverty can be shown by any one of these: a BPL card, a BPL PDS or Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card, or an RSBY card.
- Family members of a member of a registered Self Help Group (SHG) in the village are eligible.
- Families of MGNREGA workers who did at least 15 days of work in the last 12 months are eligible.
Not eligible:
- Youth younger than 15, or older than 35 (older than 45 for women and special groups), cannot join.
- Youth whose household has none of the listed poverty proofs and has not been identified as poor through the village poverty identification process are not eligible.

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — Benefits
aliases: दीन दयाल उपाध्याय ग्रामीण कौशल्य योजना
text:
- Training is completely free: there are no fees for registration, training, exams, certification or placement.
- Courses last 3 to 12 months (576 to 2,304 hours), including on-the-job training at a workplace.
- Free uniform, books and study material; free food and stay in residential courses.
- A government-recognised certificate after passing the final assessment (at least 70% marks needed).
- Help to get a job with regular monthly wages at or above minimum wages, and help to move to a new city if the job needs it.
- After placement, a monthly post-placement support amount is paid into the candidate's bank account for some months (older rule: Rs 1,000 a month for 2 to 6 months; DDU-GKY 2.0 draft procedures: Rs 1,270 a month for 6 months).

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — How to apply
aliases: दीन दयाल उपाध्याय ग्रामीण कौशल्य योजना
text:
- Register as a candidate on the Ministry of Rural Development's Kaushal Panjee mobile app or website.
- Or contact your Gram Panchayat or Gram Rozgar Sevak, who can refer you to a nearby DDU-GKY training centre; you can also approach a training centre directly.
- The training centre counsels you and tests your aptitude before you are placed in a training batch.

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) — Documents needed
aliases: दीन दयाल उपाध्याय ग्रामीण कौशल्य योजना
text:
- Proof of age and identity, such as a birth certificate.
- Any one household poverty proof: BPL card, BPL PDS or AAY card, RSBY card, MGNREGA job card showing at least 15 days of work in the last 12 months, or an NRLM Self Help Group certificate.
- SC/ST certificate or disability certificate if joining under a reserved category; minority status by self-declaration.
- Training centres help candidates who do not have Aadhaar or a bank account in their own name to get them.

title: e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Overview
text:
A free, one-time registration for unorganised workers aged 16 and above. It gives a 12-digit UAN e-Shram card and a single window for linked welfare schemes such as PMSBY accident insurance and the PM-SYM pension. Registering does not by itself pay any cash.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Labour and Employment.

title: e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Works in the unorganised sector as a home-based worker, self-employed worker or wage worker. This also covers someone in an organised-sector job who is not covered by EPFO or ESIC and is not a government employee.
- Aged 16 years or older at the time of registration.
- Not a member of EPFO or ESIC.
- Not a member of the government-funded National Pension System (NPS).
- Not an income tax payer.
- Has an Aadhaar number and a mobile number, preferably linked with Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Members of EPFO or ESIC cannot register.
- Members of the government-funded NPS cannot register.
- Income tax payers cannot register.
- Government employees are not counted as unorganised workers.
- Persons below 16 years of age cannot register.

title: e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Benefits
text:
- Free registration and a 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) e-Shram card that never expires and needs no renewal.
- One-stop access to 15 social security and welfare schemes, such as PM-SYM, PMSBY, PMJJBY, NSAP, One Nation One Ration Card and PMAY-G.
- Can enrol in PMSBY through the portal. It pays Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or permanent disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for a premium of Rs 20 a year.
- Can enrol in PMJJBY through the portal. It gives Rs 2 lakh life cover for death from any cause, for a premium of Rs 436 a year.
- Eligible workers can join PM-SYM, which gives a minimum assured pension of Rs 3,000 a month after age 60.
- Links to jobs on the National Career Service portal, and to skilling and apprenticeships on the Skill India Digital Hub.

title: e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — How to apply
text:
- Self-register online on the e-Shram portal (register.eshram.gov.in) using Aadhaar e-KYC, or through the UMANG mobile app.
- Or register at the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or State Seva Kendra. State Government field officers also help at district and sub-district level.
- Registration is free of cost, and no agency or centre may charge a fee.
- Helpline: 14434 or 1800-889-6811 (9 am to 6 pm every day, including Sundays). Grievances can be filed at gms.eshram.gov.in.

title: e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Documents needed
text:
- Aadhaar number (for Aadhaar e-KYC).
- Mobile number, preferably linked with Aadhaar.
- Savings bank account number with IFSC code.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Overview
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय अपंगता पेंशन योजना
myScheme Hindi uses इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विकलांग पेंशन योजना
text:
A monthly central pension for people aged 18 or above with severe (80% or more) or multiple disabilities from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय अपंगता पेंशन योजना
myScheme Hindi uses इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विकलांग पेंशन योजना
text:
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If the name is missing from the BPL list but the person is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave them out and to check and establish eligibility.
Not eligible:
- People from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- A certified disability below 80% does not meet the central scheme's severity level, unless the person has multiple disabilities; some states run their own disability pensions with different rules.
- The pension can be stopped after the yearly verification if the household is no longer BPL or the person has moved away; it can be restored on appeal if they become eligible again.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Benefits
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय अपंगता पेंशन योजना
myScheme Hindi uses इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विकलांग पेंशन योजना
text:
- Central pension of Rs 300 a month from age 18 to 79.
- Central pension of Rs 500 a month from age 80 onwards.
- States are urged to add at least an equal amount from their own funds, so the total pension differs from state to state.
- Paid preferably every month into a bank or post office account; no one should be denied the pension only because they have no bank account or Aadhaar number.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — How to apply
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय अपंगता पेंशन योजना
myScheme Hindi uses इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विकलांग पेंशन योजना
text:
- Fill the NSAP application form and submit it at your Gram Panchayat (in villages) or Municipality or ward office (in towns).
- States are told to hold disability camps, with free transport, where disability certificates are issued on the spot.
- The application is verified, discussed in the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha, and approved by the Block or Municipality level Sanctioning Authority; the whole process should not take more than 60 days.
- If the application is rejected, a first appeal can be made to the Appellate Authority and a second appeal to the Reviewing Authority named by the state.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Documents needed
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय अपंगता पेंशन योजना
myScheme Hindi uses इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विकलांग पेंशन योजना
text:
- Disability certificate showing the type and level of disability.
- Proof of age: birth certificate or school certificate; if not available, ration card or voter ID (EPIC); if none of these, an age certificate from a government hospital medical officer.
- BPL details of the household (BPL family ID number).
- Aadhaar number, voter ID number and ration card number, if available.
- Bank or post office account details (if available) and a photograph.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) — Overview
text:
A monthly pension for people aged 60 or more from households below the poverty line (BPL). The centre pays Rs 200 a month from age 60 to 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80, and most states add their own top-up.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Rural Development).

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Aged 60 years or more.
- Belongs to a household below the poverty line (BPL), as identified by the State or UT.
- If an eligible person's name is missing from the BPL list, the guidelines say they should not be left out; their eligibility can be checked and they can be added (following a Supreme Court direction).
- Every person aged 60 or more in a BPL family can get the pension, so more than one member of the same family can get it.
Not eligible:
- People under 60 years of age (they may fit other NSAP pensions, such as the widow or disability pension).
- People from households that are not below the poverty line are not covered by the central scheme; some states run their own pensions for them.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) — Benefits
text:
- Central pension of Rs 200 per month for ages 60 to 79.
- Rs 500 per month from age 80 onwards.
- States are urged to add at least an equal amount, so the actual monthly pension is usually higher and differs from state to state.
- Paid preferably into a bank or post office account, ideally every month; some states pay quarterly or half-yearly in advance.
- Each pensioner gets a pension passbook showing the sanction and payment details.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) — How to apply
text:
- Apply through the Gram Panchayat (villages) or Municipality (towns), or the state's social welfare or pension department; application forms should be free.
- Online applications can be made through the NSAP 'SAMBAL' mobile app or the state's pension portal.
- The application is checked, discussed in the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha, and sanctioned at block or municipality level; a decision should come within 60 days.
- If the application is rejected, the reason must be given, and the applicant can file a first appeal and then a second appeal to authorities named by the state.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) — Documents needed
text:
- Age proof: birth certificate or school certificate; if these are not available, ration card or voter ID (EPIC); if there is no valid document, an age certificate from a government hospital medical officer.
- Proof that the household is in the BPL list.
- Bank or post office savings account details.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Overview
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विधवा पेंशन योजना
text:
A monthly central pension for widows aged 40 or above from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top, so the total paid varies by state.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Eligibility rules
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विधवा पेंशन योजना
text:
- Must be a widow.
- Aged 40 years or above.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If her name is missing from the BPL list but she is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave her out and to check and establish her eligibility.
- A widow living with AIDS can be covered even if her household is not BPL, provided none of the exclusions below apply to her.
Not eligible:
- Widows from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme, except the special case of widows living with AIDS.
- A widow living with AIDS who is not BPL is still excluded if she has a government job, owns 5 acres or more of land, or owns a four-wheeler for her own use.
- The pension can be stopped after the yearly verification if the household is no longer BPL or if she has moved away; it can be restored on appeal if she becomes eligible again.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Benefits
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विधवा पेंशन योजना
text:
- Central pension of Rs 300 a month from age 40 to 79.
- Central pension of Rs 500 a month from age 80 onwards.
- States are urged to add at least an equal amount from their own funds, so the total pension differs from state to state.
- Paid preferably every month into a bank or post office account; no one should be denied the pension only because she has no bank account or Aadhaar number.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — How to apply
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विधवा पेंशन योजना
text:
- Fill the NSAP application form and submit it at your Gram Panchayat (in villages) or Municipality or ward office (in towns); forms are meant to be free and also available on state websites.
- The application is verified, discussed in the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha, and then approved by the Block or Municipality level Sanctioning Authority, which issues a sanction order and a pension passbook.
- The whole process from application to sanction or rejection should not take more than 60 days.
- If the application is rejected, a first appeal can be made to the Appellate Authority and a second appeal to the Reviewing Authority named by the state.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Documents needed
aliases: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय विधवा पेंशन योजना
text:
- Proof of age: birth certificate or school certificate; if not available, ration card or voter ID (EPIC); if none of these, an age certificate from a government hospital medical officer.
- Proof of widowhood: the husband's death certificate showing her name, or a certificate from the Revenue Authority named by the state.
- BPL details of the household (BPL family ID number).
- Aadhaar number, voter ID number and ration card number, if available.
- Bank or post office account details (if available) and a photograph.

title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) — Overview
text:
Makes childbirth, including caesarean section, and care for pregnancy complications completely free in government health facilities. This includes free medicines, tests, blood, food and transport. Sick newborns and infants up to 1 year of age get similar free care in public facilities.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (National Health Mission).

title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Any pregnant woman who gives birth in a public (government) health institution.
- Pregnant women and new mothers with complications before or after delivery who are treated in a public health institution (added in 2014).
- Sick newborns and infants up to 1 year of age who are treated in a public health institution.
- It covers all pregnant women using public health institutions, not only poor or BPL families.
Not eligible:
- Deliveries and treatment in private hospitals are not covered.

title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) — Benefits
text:
- Delivery is completely free, including caesarean section, with no user charges of any kind.
- Free medicines and consumables, and free essential tests such as blood and urine tests and ultrasound.
- Free food during the hospital stay: up to 3 days after a normal delivery and up to 7 days after a caesarean section.
- Free blood when it is needed.
- Free transport from home to the hospital, between hospitals if referred, and a free drop back home after a 48 hours stay.
- Sick newborns and infants get the same kind of free treatment, medicines, tests, blood and transport.

title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) — How to apply
text:
- No application form is needed; go to any government health facility (sub-centre, PHC, CHC, district hospital) for delivery or treatment.
- Ask your ASHA or ANM to help arrange the free transport to the facility.
- If anyone asks you to pay, you can complain through the grievance redressal system the state must set up under the scheme.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Overview
text:
A cash payment under the National Health Mission for pregnant women who give birth in a government health facility or an accredited private hospital. In the 10 Low Performing States every woman delivering in a government facility qualifies; in other states it is for BPL, SC and ST women. The scheme is still running.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (National Health Mission).

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
text:
- You must be a pregnant woman who gives birth in a health facility: a sub-centre, PHC, CHC, FRU, the general ward of a district or state hospital, or an accredited private institution.
- In the 10 Low Performing States (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Rajasthan, Odisha, Jammu and Kashmir), every pregnant woman who delivers in a government health centre qualifies.
- In all other states and UTs (called High Performing States), only women from BPL, Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe families qualify.
- In every state, BPL, SC and ST women also qualify if they deliver in an accredited private institution, but they must show a BPL or SC/ST certificate and a referral slip.
- In the Low Performing States there is no age limit and no limit on the number of births for delivery in a government or accredited facility.
Not eligible:
- In the High Performing States, women who are not BPL, SC or ST do not get the cash payment.
- Births in a private hospital that is not accredited for JSY are not covered.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
text: - The government does not pay the bill of a private hospital; a woman who chooses an accredited private hospital gets only her fixed cash amount.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Benefits
text:
- In the Low Performing States, a mother in a rural area gets Rs 1,400 for giving birth in a health facility.
- In the Low Performing States, a mother in an urban area gets Rs 1,000.
- In the High Performing States, an eligible mother gets Rs 700 in a rural area and Rs 600 in an urban area.
- The cash is meant to be paid in full at the health facility at the time of delivery.
- A BPL woman aged 19 years or more who gives birth at home gets Rs 500 per delivery, for up to 2 live births (older rule; see status note).
- The ASHA worker who helps the mother gets her own separate payment (Rs 600 in rural areas, Rs 400 in urban areas); this is separate from the mother's amount.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — How to apply
text:
- Register your pregnancy early with your ASHA, ANM or anganwadi worker; you will get a JSY card together with the Mother and Child Health (MCH) card.
- Go to a government health centre or an accredited private hospital for the delivery; the cash is handed over at the facility.
- If you go to an accredited private hospital, or deliver away from your usual home, carry a referral slip from your ASHA, ANM or medical officer.
- Complaints about eligibility, amount or delay can be taken to the grievance cell set up in each district.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Documents needed
text:
- JSY card together with the Mother and Child Health (MCH) card.
- BPL certificate (needed in High Performing States and for home delivery); where BPL cards are not issued, the state may let the gram pradhan or ward member certify the family as poor.
- SC or ST certificate, if claiming on that basis.
- Referral slip from the ASHA, ANM or medical officer when delivering in an accredited private institution or away from home.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Overview
text:
A revolving bank loan account with a RuPay card that farmers, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, livestock keepers and fishers can use for farming costs. Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, short-term loans up to Rs 3 lakh carry 7% interest, which drops to 4% if repaid on time.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Credit Division); loans given by banks under RBI rules.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Farmers who own and cultivate land, either alone or jointly.
- Tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers.
- Self Help Groups or Joint Liability Groups of farmers, including groups of tenant farmers and sharecroppers.
- Dairy, poultry, sheep, goat, pig and rabbit farmers with their own, rented or leased sheds, individually, jointly or in groups.
- Fishers and fish farmers who own or lease a pond, tank, open water body, hatchery or registered fishing boat and hold the required fishing licence.
Not eligible:
- Only one KCC per farmer: the application asks you to declare that you have no KCC from another bank branch.
- If you already have a combined KCC for crops and allied activities, a separate livestock or fisheries KCC is not issued; the existing limit is raised instead.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Benefits
text:
- Short-term loans up to Rs 3 lakh for crops and allied activities at 7% interest a year, because the government pays banks a 1.5% interest subvention.
- Repay on time and you get a further 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive, so the effective interest becomes 4% a year.
- For a KCC used only for animal husbandry or fisheries, the interest benefit covers loans up to Rs 2 lakh, within the overall Rs 3 lakh.
- No collateral security or margin is needed for agricultural loans up to Rs 2 lakh (from 1 January 2025).
- Each bank decides how long the Kisan Credit Card stays valid and when it is reviewed. The credit limit itself is set for five years. The card is a smart card that also works as a debit card, and the bank may issue it as a RuPay or EMV chip card. Farmers can draw money at the bank branch, by cheque, at ATMs, through bank agents (business correspondents), on PoS machines at input dealers, and through mobile banking.
- The credit limit is based on the crop's scale of finance times the area farmed, plus 10% for household and post-harvest needs and 20% for farm asset upkeep, and it rises by 10% each year.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — How to apply
text:
- Fill in the KCC application form at a bank branch in your area: a public sector, private, regional rural, small finance or cooperative bank.
- PM-KISAN beneficiaries can use a simple one-page KCC form at the bank branch where they receive PM-KISAN money.
- For a livestock or fisheries KCC, the bank should issue the card within 15 days of a complete application, and processing fees are waived for limits up to Rs 3 lakh.
- For help with a livestock KCC, you can also contact the State Animal Husbandry Department.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Documents needed
text:
- Identity proof such as Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN card, driving licence or passport.
- Address proof such as Aadhaar, Voter ID, passport or a recent electricity or telephone bill.
- Recent passport-size photographs.
- Land records, or details of land you farm as owner, lessee or sharecropper.
- For livestock or fisheries: details of the animals or birds, the shed or pond, and the fishing licence where needed.

title: Mission Vatsalya – Sponsorship Support (non-institutional care) (Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship) — Overview
text:
Under Mission Vatsalya, a vulnerable child living with their own family or relatives can get Rs 4,000 a month for schooling, health and food, so the child does not have to be placed in a children's home. Each case is checked and approved in the district: the District Child Protection Unit and a district committee recommend it, and the District Magistrate approves it.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

title: Mission Vatsalya – Sponsorship Support (non-institutional care) (Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
text:
- The child must be under 18. Sponsorship can continue only until the child turns 18.
- A child whose mother is widowed, divorced, or abandoned by the family.
- An orphaned child living with relatives (extended family).
- A child whose parents have a life-threatening or terminal illness, or cannot care for the child either financially or physically.
- A child in need of care and protection under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015. Examples: homeless, hit by a natural disaster, child labour, child marriage, trafficked, affected by HIV/AIDS, disabled, missing or runaway, begging or living on the street, or abused.
- A child covered under the PM CARES for Children Scheme.
- For preventive sponsorship (help so the child can stay in the family), family income must not be above Rs 72,000 a year in rural areas or Rs 96,000 a year in other areas.
- A child in a children's home can also be sent back to the family with sponsorship, if the Child Welfare Committee or Juvenile Justice Board recommends it.
Not eligible:
- Sponsorship stops if the child has to be placed in a children's home.

title: Mission Vatsalya – Sponsorship Support (non-institutional care) (Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
text: - Sponsorship is reviewed and stopped for a time if a school-going child is irregular at school for more than 30 days. This does not apply to children with special needs.

title: Mission Vatsalya – Sponsorship Support (non-institutional care) (Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship) — Benefits
text:
- Rs 4,000 per month for each child.
- The money is paid every month into a bank or post office account in the child's name. The guardian, preferably the mother, runs the account.
- The district committee decides how long sponsorship lasts, case by case. Continuing it up to age 18 needs written reasons from the Juvenile Justice Board, Child Welfare Committee or Children's Court.
- The District Child Protection Unit may arrange a yearly health check-up for the child, and its workers visit the home and school every quarter.
- State governments may add their own extra money on top.

title: Mission Vatsalya – Sponsorship Support (non-institutional care) (Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship) — How to apply
text:
- Contact the District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) in your district. DCPU workers, the Gram Panchayat and the Urban Ward Committee also find needy families.
- The DCPU or the child's family can upload the request on the Mission Vatsalya portal.
- The Sponsorship and Foster Care Approval Committee usually meets in the first week of each quarter and recommends cases. The District Magistrate gives final approval.
- If a child is in danger or needs care urgently, call the Child Helpline 1098.

title: Mission Vatsalya – Sponsorship Support (non-institutional care) (Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship) — Documents needed
text:
- The national guidelines do not give a fixed list of documents. Ask the District Child Protection Unit what papers your state needs.
- For an extension, the committee looks at the child's yearly health check-up report and a report from home and school visits.

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) — Overview
aliases: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
text:
Helps young people aged 14 to 35 learn a trade as apprentices in companies. The employer pays a monthly stipend, and the Central Government pays 25% of it (up to Rs 1,500 a month) straight into the apprentice's bank account. NAPS-2 formally ended on 31 March 2026 and ran on a temporary extension to 30 September 2026 while its successor (PM-NAPS 3.0) awaits approval, so check its current status.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
aliases: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
text:
- Aged 14 to 35 years (the age group the Central Government support is designed for).
- At least 14 years old, or at least 18 years old for training in hazardous industries.
- Has passed at least Class 5 (for optional trades) and has the education, technical and physical fitness standards set for the chosen trade.
- Has an Aadhaar number and is registered on the Apprenticeship Training Portal.
- Has signed a contract of apprenticeship with an establishment, and the contract is registered on the portal.
- Can be an ITI pass-out, a graduate or diploma holder, someone who finished an NSQF-aligned course (such as PMKVY), a student pursuing graduation or a diploma, or a fresher.
Not eligible:
- The Central Government's share of the stipend is paid only for a person's first apprenticeship training.
- A person can do at most two apprenticeship trainings, and the second cannot be in the same trade.
- There must be a gap of at least one year between two apprenticeship trainings after a completed training (some exceptions apply, for example when the employer was at fault).

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
aliases: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
text: - A person whose earlier apprenticeship contract was ended because they did not follow its terms cannot get another apprenticeship contract.

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) — Benefits
aliases: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
text:
- The Central Government pays 25% of the stipend, up to Rs 1,500 per month, directly to the apprentice by DBT during training.
- The employer pays the rest of the stipend; from 11 September 2025 the minimum monthly stipend is Rs 6,800 for Class 5 to 9 pass, Rs 8,200 for Class 10 pass, and Rs 9,600 for Class 12 pass, National or State certificate holders, and vocational (technician vocational) apprentices.
- The minimum monthly stipend is Rs 10,900 for technician apprentices or diploma holders and Rs 12,300 for graduate or degree apprentices.
- Hands-on on-the-job training at a real workplace; freshers without prior training first get basic training.

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) — How to apply
aliases: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
text:
- Register as a candidate on the Apprenticeship Training Portal (apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) and complete Aadhaar e-KYC.
- Search apprenticeship openings posted by companies, apply, and accept an offer online.
- Sign the apprenticeship contract online with the company; training is counted from the date the contract is registered on the portal.

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) — Documents needed
aliases: Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
text:
- Aadhaar number (or a Unique Identification Number for some Jammu & Kashmir and North-East candidates).
- Certificates of the education or technical qualification required for the trade.
- Bank account details to receive the government's share of the stipend by DBT.

title: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — Overview
text:
A one-time lump sum of Rs 20,000 paid to a below-poverty-line (BPL) household when its main earner dies aged 18 to 59, whatever the cause of death.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

title: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — Eligibility rules
text:
- The household must be below the poverty line (BPL).
- The person who died must have been the household's main earner (breadwinner).
- The breadwinner must have been aged 18 to 59 years at the time of death.
- Any death counts, whether natural, accidental or from any other cause.
- A woman who was a homemaker also counts as a breadwinner.
- The money is paid to the surviving family member who, after a local inquiry, is found to be the new head of the household.
- Household means the spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters and dependent parents; if the person who died was an unmarried adult, it means minor brothers and sisters and dependent parents.
Not eligible:
- Households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- Deaths of a breadwinner aged 60 or above, or below 18, are not covered.
- The scheme pays only on the death of the breadwinner, not of other family members.

title: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — Benefits
text:
- A one-time lump sum of Rs 20,000 to the bereaved household.
- The help is meant to be given in every case where a family's breadwinner dies.
- Payment is preferably made into a bank or post office account.

title: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — How to apply
text:
- Fill the NFBS application form and submit it at your Gram Panchayat (in villages) or Municipality or ward office (in towns).
- The application is verified, discussed in the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha, and then the Block or Municipality level Sanctioning Authority issues a sanction order for the payment.
- The whole process from application to sanction or rejection should not take more than 60 days.
- If the application is rejected, a first appeal can be made to the Appellate Authority and a second appeal to the Reviewing Authority named by the state.

title: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) — Documents needed
text:
- Details of the person who died: name, age at the time of death, address and the household's BPL family ID.
- Details of the applicant (the new head of household): name, address and date of birth with proof.
- Proof of age such as a birth or school certificate; if not available, ration card or voter ID (EPIC).
- Bank or post office account details, since payment is preferably made into an account.

title: National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Overview
text:
Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, every member of a household that the state identifies as a Priority Household gets 5 kg of foodgrains a month from the ration shop. Under PMGKAY this grain is free of cost, and the Centre has continued it for five years from 1 January 2024. States decide which households qualify, within coverage limits of up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban people nationally.
Central government scheme. Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

title: National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- The household must be identified by its State/UT government as a Priority Household (PHH) and hold an NFSA ration card.
- Each state sets its own criteria for priority households, so the rules differ from state to state.
- Nationally, up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population can be covered; each state has its own coverage percentage.
- The eldest woman of the household aged 18 years or more is named head of the household on the ration card; if there is no such woman, the eldest man is head until a female member turns 18.
- The Centre has told states to include eligible persons with disabilities, persons affected by leprosy and children born after 2011.
Not eligible:
- Households not identified by the state as priority households or Antyodaya households are not covered.
- Total coverage in each state is fixed using Census 2011 figures; the ceiling can be raised only after data from the next census is published.
- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards, and members who have died or migrated, are removed when states verify their lists.

title: National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Benefits
text:
- Every member of a priority household is entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains (rice, wheat or coarse grains) per person per month.
- Under PMGKAY the grain is given free of cost, so there is nothing to pay at the ration shop.
- Free grain started on 1 January 2023, and the Centre decided to continue it for five years starting 1 January 2024.
- The prices fixed in the Act before free distribution were Rs 3 per kg for rice, Rs 2 per kg for wheat and Rs 1 per kg for coarse grains.
- Under One Nation One Ration Card, the grain can be taken from any ePoS-enabled ration shop in India.
- If the state does not supply the entitled grain, the person can claim a food security allowance from the state government.

title: National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — How to apply
text:
- Apply for a ration card at the Food and Civil Supplies office of your State/UT; the central department does not issue ration cards.
- The state checks your household against its priority-household criteria and, if you qualify within its coverage limit, issues a PHH ration card.
- Collect grain at your fair price (ration) shop with your existing NFSA ration card; no separate card is needed for PMGKAY, and any household member can collect it.
- For complaints, use your state helpline or the District Grievance Redressal Officer, and appeal to the State Food Commission if needed. The department lists toll-free number 1967 and Anna Sahayata IVRS 14457.

title: National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Documents needed
text:
- NFSA priority household (PHH) ration card to collect grain.
- Identity is checked at the ration shop by Aadhaar-based fingerprint or iris scan, or by Aadhaar OTP or PDS OTP.
- If Aadhaar authentication fails, or Aadhaar is missing or not linked, one of 8 alternative identity documents notified on 08.02.2017 can be used; genuine beneficiaries should not be refused grain.
- The documents needed for a new ration card are decided by your state government.

title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Overview
text:
Gives every TB patient registered (notified) on the Ni-kshay portal money every month for nutritious food for the whole time they are on TB treatment, paid by direct bank transfer. The amount was raised from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 per month in late 2024.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Central TB Division, National TB Elimination Programme).

title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- You must be a TB (tuberculosis) patient who is notified (registered) on the Ni-kshay portal.
- Patients treated in the private sector qualify too, as long as they are notified on Ni-kshay.
- New, previously treated and drug-resistant TB patients are all covered.
- There is no age or income limit; all notified TB patients are beneficiaries.
- Children with TB are covered; if the child has no bank account, the money goes to a parent's or guardian's account.
- Patients notified on or after 1 April 2018, and those already on treatment on that date, are eligible.
Not eligible:
- A TB patient who is not notified on the Ni-kshay portal cannot receive the payment.
- Payments are only for the period the patient is on anti-TB treatment; they stop when treatment ends.

title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Benefits
text:
- Rs 1,000 per month for as long as the patient is on TB treatment (raised from Rs 500 per month; increase announced in late 2024).
- Money is paid by Direct Benefit Transfer into the bank account, preferably an Aadhaar-linked account.
- Under the 2018 payment schedule, the first payment comes when the patient is notified, and later payments come at follow-up points during treatment (for a new patient: at about 2 months and at the end of 6 months).
- If treatment is extended, payment continues for the extra months.
- Some states may give a food basket of at least the same value instead of cash, with central approval.

title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — How to apply
text:
- There is no separate application; the doctor or facility treating your TB notifies you on the Ni-kshay portal.
- Give your bank account and Aadhaar details to the TB health staff so they can be entered on Ni-kshay.
- If you have no bank account, health staff will help you open one, preferably under Jan Dhan Yojana, and help with Aadhaar enrolment.
- Call the Ni-kshay helpline 1800-11-6666 for help.

title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Documents needed
text:
- Bank account details of the patient (or of a parent or guardian for a child).
- Aadhaar number (preferred for payment; health staff help with enrolment if you do not have one).
- TB diagnosis notified on the Ni-kshay portal by the treating facility.

title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Overview
text:
A central scholarship of Rs 12,000 a year for bright students from low-income families studying in Class 9 to 12 in government, government-aided and local body schools. Students are chosen through a state-level test taken in Class 8, and 1,00,000 new scholarships are given every year.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy.

title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
text:
- Parents' income from all sources must be no more than Rs 3,50,000 a year.
- You need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 7 exam to sit the selection test. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must study as a regular student in a government, government-aided or local body school.
- You must pass the state's selection test in Class 8 (Mental Ability Test and Scholastic Aptitude Test) with at least 40% marks in aggregate. The cut-off for SC/ST students is 32%.
- At the time of selection you need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 8 exam. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must be promoted from Class 8 to Class 9 to start receiving the scholarship.
- To continue, you must pass Class 9 and Class 11 in the first attempt, and you need at least 60% marks in Class 10 (5% lower for SC/ST students).
Not eligible:
- Students of Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.
- Students of residential schools run by Central or State Government institutions that provide boarding, lodging and education.
- Students of private schools.
- Diploma or certificate-level courses and studies abroad are not covered.

title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
text:
- A student can hold only one Central Government scholarship.
- The scholarship stops if there is a gap of one academic session, and once stopped it cannot be restarted.

title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Benefits
text:
- Rs 12,000 a year (Rs 1,000 a month) for each selected student.
- Paid for up to four years, from Class 9 to Class 12.
- 1,00,000 fresh scholarships every year, divided among States and UTs by a fixed quota.
- The money is sent directly to the student's bank account through DBT.

title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — How to apply
text:
- While in Class 8, take the NMMSS selection test (MAT and SAT) conducted by your State/UT education department, usually around November.
- If selected, create a One Time Registration (OTR) on the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) and apply for the fresh scholarship.
- Your school verifies the application, then the State nodal officer approves it.
- Apply for renewal on NSP every year within the deadline, or the scholarship is discontinued.

title: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Documents needed
text:
- Income certificate of the parent or guardian, issued by the competent State/UT authority.
- Caste certificate, if applicable.
- Aadhaar number and a mobile number linked with Aadhaar (for OTR).
- Bank account in the student's name, preferably in SBI or another core-banking bank.

title: National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders) — Overview
aliases: व्यापारियों के लिए राष्ट्रीय पेंशन योजना
Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana
text:
A voluntary pension scheme for small shopkeepers, retail traders and self-employed people aged 18 to 40 whose yearly turnover is Rs 1.5 crore or less. The trader pays a small monthly amount, the government pays the same amount, and the trader gets a pension of at least Rs 3,000 a month from age 60.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Labour and Employment.

title: National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders) — Eligibility rules
aliases: व्यापारियों के लिए राष्ट्रीय पेंशन योजना
Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana
text:
- Self-employed shop owner, retail trader or similar small businessperson, for example a rice or oil mill owner, workshop owner, commission agent, real estate broker, or small hotel or restaurant owner.
- Aged 18 to 40 when joining.
- Annual business turnover of not more than Rs 1.5 crore.
- Has an Aadhaar card and a savings bank or Jan Dhan account with IFSC.
Not eligible:
- People older than 40 cannot join.
- Income tax payers cannot join.
- Members of EPFO, ESIC or the government-funded NPS cannot join.
- People already enrolled in PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) or PM Kisan Maan-dhan cannot join.

title: National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders) — Benefits
aliases: व्यापारियों के लिए राष्ट्रीय पेंशन योजना
Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana
text:
- A minimum assured pension of Rs 3,000 per month from age 60.
- The trader pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month depending on age at joining (Rs 55 at 18, Rs 200 at 40) until age 60, and the Central Government adds an equal amount.
- If the pensioner dies, the spouse gets 50% of the pension as family pension; family pension is only for the spouse.
- If the member dies before 60 after paying regularly, the spouse can continue the scheme or take back the member's share with interest.
- Leaving within 10 years returns only the trader's own contribution with savings bank interest; leaving after 10 years but before 60 returns it with the interest earned by the fund or savings bank interest, whichever is higher. The government's share is not paid out on exit.

title: National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders) — How to apply
aliases: व्यापारियों के लिए राष्ट्रीय पेंशन योजना
Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana
text:
- Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) and enrol using Aadhaar and a savings or Jan Dhan bank account on self-declaration, or self-enrol on the official portal maandhan.in.
- The first contribution is paid in cash at the CSC; later contributions are auto-debited monthly (quarterly, half-yearly or yearly payment is also allowed).
- Enrolment is free; if payments stop, the account can be revived by paying the dues with a small interest charge.
- Helpline: 14434 or 1800 2676 888.

title: National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders) — Documents needed
aliases: व्यापारियों के लिए राष्ट्रीय पेंशन योजना
Pradhan Mantri Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan Yojana
text:
- Aadhaar card (the date of birth in Aadhaar is used and cannot be changed later).
- Savings bank or Jan Dhan account number with IFSC.
- Self-declaration of eligibility.

title: NPS Vatsalya — Overview
text:
A long-term savings and pension account under the National Pension System that a parent or guardian opens in the name of a child under 18, with as little as Rs 250 a year. When the child turns 18, they can move the money to a regular NPS account or take part of it out, and they can withdraw it all if the total is less than Rs 8 lakh.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services); regulated and administered by PFRDA.

title: NPS Vatsalya — Eligibility rules
text:
- The child must be below 18 years of age (17 or younger) when the account is opened.
- Open to Indian citizens under 18, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).
- A parent or legal guardian opens and runs the account in the child's name. The child is the only beneficiary.
- The minimum contribution is Rs 250 to open the account and at least Rs 250 in each financial year. There is no upper limit.
- For an NRI or OCI child, a bank account must be given (the minor's own or joint NRE/NRO account).
Not eligible:
- Anyone who has already turned 18 cannot open an NPS Vatsalya account. They can join the regular NPS instead.

title: NPS Vatsalya — Benefits
text:
- A pension fund registered with PFRDA, chosen by the guardian, invests the money. Returns are market-linked, with an indicative 50% to 75% in equity.
- Partial withdrawals are allowed only after 3 years from opening the account. You can take out up to 25% of the money paid in (not the returns) for the child's education, treatment of specified illnesses, or disability of more than 75%.
- Up to 2 partial withdrawals are allowed before age 18. After completing KYC, 2 more are allowed between ages 18 and 21.
- At 18 the account can continue for up to 3 more years. After fresh KYC, the young person has three choices: move the full amount into regular NPS (All Citizen Model), take up to 80% as a lump sum and use the rest to buy an annuity, or withdraw everything if the total is less than Rs 8 lakh.
- If no choice is made by age 21, the account moves to a higher-equity scheme of the same pension fund and follows regular NPS rules.
- If the child dies, the entire amount saved is paid to the guardian, nominee or legal heirs.
