aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for SC students
text:
- Caste certificate signed by the authorised officer.
- Valid income certificate from the authority named by the State. For courses longer than one year it is needed only once, at admission.
- Certificates or mark sheets of all exams passed.
- Passport-size photograph.
- Aadhaar number (Aadhaar authentication is compulsory at renewal) and an Aadhaar-linked bank account.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — Overview
aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
text:
Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe students studying from Class 11 up to post-graduation in India whose family income is Rs 2.5 lakh a year or less. It pays compulsory course fees plus a monthly stipend, and is run by state and UT governments with central funding.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
text:
- Belongs to a Scheduled Tribe notified for the student's own (domicile) state or union territory.
- Has passed Class 10 (matriculation) or a higher exam and is studying a recognised post-matric course, from Class 11 up to post-graduation, in India.
- Family income from all sources must be Rs 2,50,000 a year or less (income of the father and mother is counted; earnings of siblings or other relatives are not).
- An orphan supported by a guardian does not have to meet the income limit.
- Has a bank account in the student's own name, linked to Aadhaar and a mobile number.
- Does not hold any other scholarship at the same time; if offered another one, the student must choose one of them.
- The course must be at a recognised institution, such as a government college or university, a recognised private university or professional college, a Class 11-12 school, a polytechnic or an ITI.
Not eligible:
- Students admitted to one of the Ministry's listed top class institutes (252 at the time of the guidelines) are covered by the National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students instead of this scheme.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
text:
- A student who has finished a course in one stream cannot get the scholarship for a course at the same level in another stream (for example B.Com after B.A.).
- A student who fails a year gets no scholarship until they pass that class and are promoted.
- Self-declared income or affidavits are not accepted as proof of income.
- Scholarship can be cancelled if it was obtained through false information, or if the student changes course or institution without state approval.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — Benefits
aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
text:
- Compulsory non-refundable course fees are paid as fixed by the state's fee fixation committee; for private institutes the central support is capped at Rs 2.50 lakh a year for engineering, Rs 6.00 lakh a year for MBBS/MS/MD and Rs 1.00 lakh a year for other courses.
- Monthly stipend for students living in a hostel: Rs 1,200 for Group I (professional degree, PG diploma, MPhil/PhD), Rs 820 for Group II (general degrees such as BA, BSc, BCom, MA), Rs 570 for Group III (ITI, polytechnic diploma, vocational) and Rs 380 for Group IV (Class 11 and 12).
- Monthly stipend for day scholars: Rs 550 for Group I, Rs 530 for Group II, Rs 300 for Group III and Rs 230 for Group IV.
- The stipend is paid for up to 10 months in a year.
- Students with disabilities get an extra Rs 800 a month if they live in a hostel, or Rs 600 a month as day scholars.
- Money is sent directly to the student's bank account (DBT); states may pay more than these rates from their own funds.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — How to apply
aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
text:
- Apply online on the scholarship portal of your home (domicile) state or UT; some states use the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) instead.
- If you study in another state, still apply to your home state; you can join any government institute, but a private institute must be on your state's approved (empanelled) list.
- The suggested registration window is 1 April to 30 September; your institute checks the application first, then district or state officials. Actual dates differ by state.
- Renew every year after passing and moving to the next class.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes for Studies in India (PMS-ST) — Documents needed
aliases: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
text:
- Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-linked bank account in the student's name.
- ST certificate from the competent state/UT authority and a domicile certificate.
- Family income certificate from the notified authority.
- Certificates and marksheets of exams passed, including last qualifying marks.
- Passport-size photograph.
- Disability certificate, if claiming the disability allowance.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Overview
text:
A one-year accident insurance, renewed every year, for bank or post office account holders aged 18 to 70. It pays Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for a premium of Rs 20 a year taken automatically from the account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Aged 18 to 70 years.
- Holds an individual or joint savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- Agrees to join and allows the yearly premium to be auto-debited from that account.
- A person can be covered through only one account, even if they have several.
- In a joint account, each holder who meets the conditions can join by paying Rs 20 each.
Not eligible:
- Cover ends on reaching age 70 (age nearest birthday).
- Cover ends if the bank account is closed or does not have enough balance to pay the premium.
- Only accidents are covered; death by suicide is not covered, though murder is.
- If enrolled through more than one account, the extra premium is forfeited and cover is given through one account only.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Benefits
text:
- Rs 2 lakh on death due to an accident.
- Rs 2 lakh for total and permanent loss of both eyes, both hands or both feet, or of one eye together with one hand or foot.
- Rs 1 lakh for permanent loss of one eye or of one hand or foot (partial disability).
- The premium is Rs 20 a year, auto-debited from the account in one instalment.
- Cover lasts one year, from 1 June to 31 May, is renewed every year, and is in addition to any other insurance the person has.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — How to apply
text:
- Go to the bank branch or post office where you have your savings account and submit the scheme form with your consent for auto-debit.
- Late joining during the year is allowed on payment of the premium. If you leave the scheme, you can rejoin in a later year by paying the annual premium, and cover starts from the date the premium is debited.
- Claims are filed through the bank or post office by the insured person, or by the nominee or legal heirs. Disability amounts go to the insured person's account and death amounts to the nominee's account.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Documents needed
text:
- A savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- The filled scheme enrolment form with consent for auto-debit of the premium.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Overview
text:
Gives adult women from poor households that have no LPG connection a deposit-free cooking gas connection. The government pays Rs 2,050 towards a 14.2 kg cylinder connection, and the first refill and the stove are also free.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- The applicant must be a woman who is at least 18 years old.
- No one in the household should already have an LPG connection from any oil marketing company.
- The household must fall in one of the listed groups: SC or ST households, PMAY-Gramin beneficiaries, Most Backward Classes, Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card holders, tea and ex-tea garden tribes, forest dwellers, people living on islands or river islands, or SECC (AHL TIN) households.
- A poor household outside these groups can still qualify by giving a 14-point deprivation declaration in the set format.
- Migrant families can apply by giving a self-declaration in place of address proof and a ration card.
Not eligible:
- Households where any family member already has an LPG connection.
- Women under 18 years of age.
- Men cannot get the connection in their own name; it is issued to an adult woman of the household.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Benefits
text:
- A deposit-free LPG connection: the Government of India pays Rs 2,050 for a 14.2 kg cylinder connection or Rs 1,300 for a 5 kg cylinder connection.
- This amount covers the cylinder security deposit (Rs 1,700 for 14.2 kg or Rs 950 for 5 kg), the pressure regulator (Rs 150), the LPG hose (Rs 100), the consumer card (Rs 25) and inspection or installation charges (Rs 75).
- The first LPG refill and the stove (hotplate) are given free by the oil company along with the connection.
- The family can choose a 14.2 kg single cylinder, a 5 kg single cylinder or a 5 kg double cylinder connection.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — How to apply
text:
- Apply online through the PMUY portal (pmuy.gov.in), which links to the IndianOil, Bharat Gas and HP Gas application pages.
- Or take the filled form and documents to any nearby LPG distributor of your choice.
- Applying yourself costs nothing; a Common Service Centre (CSC) may charge Rs 20.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Documents needed
text:
- KYC application form with photo.
- Aadhaar of the applicant and of all adult family members.
- Ration card or another state government document showing the family members (migrants can give a self-declaration instead).
- Proof of address, if the address is different from the one on Aadhaar.
- Bank account number and IFSC, with passbook or cancelled cheque.
- Deprivation declaration in the prescribed format, when applying as a poor household.

title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Overview
text:
RVY gives free assisted-living devices such as walking sticks, walkers, wheelchairs, hearing aids, spectacles and dentures to senior citizens aged 60 or above who have an age-related disability or infirmity. Seniors must be from a BPL family or have a monthly income of Rs 15,000 or less.
Central government scheme. Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (implemented by ALIMCO).

title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Must be a senior citizen aged 60 years or above.
- Must belong to the BPL category, shown by a BPL ration card, proof of old age pension under IGNOAPS or a state/UT pension scheme, or a certificate from the district authority.
- Seniors who are not BPL can also apply if their monthly income from all sources is Rs 15,000 or less.
- Must have an age-related disability or infirmity, such as low vision, hearing loss, loss of teeth or difficulty in walking.
- Must have an Aadhaar card or Aadhaar enrolment slip.
- A medical officer's certificate is needed for loss of vision, hearing impairment, loss of teeth, or locomotor disability needing a wheelchair.
Not eligible:
- People below 60 years of age.
- Non-BPL seniors whose monthly income from all sources is more than Rs 15,000.
- Anyone who received the same device free from any government source (including local bodies and public undertakings) in the last 3 years.

title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Benefits
text:
- Assisted-living devices are given free of cost to eligible senior citizens.
- Devices include walking sticks, crutches, walkers, wheelchairs (including commode wheelchairs), hearing aids, spectacles, artificial dentures, knee/spinal/cervical braces, cushions and orthotic or prosthetic appliances.
- In OPD mode at ALIMCO centres, the device can be given on the same day as the assessment or on a day set by the OPD in-charge.

title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — How to apply
text:
- Attend an RVY camp in your district, where seniors are assessed and devices are then distributed.
- Or visit an ALIMCO production centre or regional marketing centre (OPD mode) to be assessed and get the device.
- Call ALIMCO's toll-free number 1800-180-5129 to find the nearest centre or camp.

title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Documents needed
text:
- Aadhaar card or Aadhaar enrolment slip.
- Proof of BPL status: BPL ration card, proof of IGNOAPS or state old age pension, or district authority certificate; or proof that monthly income is Rs 15,000 or less.
- Medical officer's certificate for loss of vision, hearing impairment, loss of teeth, or locomotor disability needing a wheelchair.

title: Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Overview
text:
Anganwadi Centres give extra food (supplementary nutrition) to children aged 6 months to 6 years, to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers, and to adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 in Aspirational Districts and North-Eastern states. There is no caste, religion or income condition; the person only has to register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

title: Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Eligibility rules
text:
- Children aged 6 months to 6 years get supplementary nutrition.
- Pregnant women, and mothers for up to 6 months after the birth.
- Adolescent girls aged 14 to 18 years, but only in Aspirational Districts and in Assam and the other North-Eastern states.
- Anyone who qualifies can join. There is no caste, religion or income condition.
- The beneficiary must register at the nearest Anganwadi Centre with Aadhaar. A child can be registered using the mother's Aadhaar.
- Families staying in an Anganwadi area, even for a short time, can register there. A registration can be moved to the new centre through Poshan Tracker.
Not eligible:
- Food is given only to people registered at an Anganwadi Centre.
- Adolescent girls outside Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern states (including Assam) are not covered.

title: Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Benefits
text:
- Food is given for at least 300 days a year, about 25 days a month.
- Children aged 3 to 6 years get a morning snack and a hot cooked meal at the Anganwadi.
- Children aged 6 months to 3 years, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, severely malnourished children and eligible adolescent girls get take-home ration (prepared food, not raw grain). It is given twice a month, preferably on the 1st and 15th.
- Daily food norm: 500 kcal and 12 to 15 g protein for children aged 6 to 72 months, and 800 kcal and 20 to 25 g protein for severely malnourished children.
- Daily food norm: 600 kcal and 18 to 20 g protein for pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and adolescent girls.
- The Anganwadi also gives pre-school education, nutrition and health education, vaccination, health check-ups and referrals to hospitals.

title: Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — How to apply
text:
- Go to the nearest Anganwadi Centre and register with the Anganwadi worker.
- Bring Aadhaar. If you do not have it, the Anganwadi worker and supervisors are supposed to help you get one.
- Your details and the food you receive are recorded on the Poshan Tracker app.

title: Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 – Supplementary Nutrition (Poshan 2.0) — Documents needed
text:
- Aadhaar of the beneficiary. For a child, the mother's Aadhaar is enough.
- A child does not need their own Aadhaar card.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Overview
aliases: Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin toilet scheme
text:
Under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), eligible rural households that do not have a toilet get Rs 12,000 to build and use one. It covers all BPL families and certain poorer APL families. The mission is now in Phase II, which mainly aims to keep villages open-defecation free, and only new eligible households get the incentive.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Jal Shakti (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation).

title: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Eligibility rules
aliases: Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin toilet scheme
text:
- All Below Poverty Line (BPL) households in rural areas.
- Above Poverty Line (APL) households that belong to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
- APL households of small and marginal farmers.
- APL landless labourers who have a homestead.
- APL households with a physically handicapped member.
- APL households headed by a woman.
- The incentive is only for new eligible households, such as new families that do not yet have a toilet.
Not eligible:
- APL households that are not in the listed groups get no incentive. They are encouraged to build a toilet with their own money.
- Households already covered earlier do not get the incentive again.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Benefits
aliases: Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin toilet scheme
text:
- An incentive of Rs 12,000 to build a household toilet. This also covers water storage for handwashing and keeping the toilet clean.
- The Centre pays Rs 7,200 (60%) and the State Rs 4,800 (40%). In North-Eastern and special-category states, the Centre pays Rs 10,800 (90%) and the State Rs 1,200 (10%).
- The money is an incentive, not a full refund. It is meant to be enough for a basic twin-pit toilet, and the family pays any extra cost.
- Families with no space for their own toilet can use Community Managed Sanitation Complexes built in the village.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — How to apply
aliases: Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin toilet scheme
text:
- Apply online using the IHHL application form on the SBM portal (sbm.gov.in), logging in with your mobile number and an OTP.
- Or ask your Gram Panchayat, which runs toilet building under the mission in the village.
- Toilet building is tracked online, and photos of the toilet are geo-tagged and uploaded through a mobile app.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) - Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) incentive (SBM-G IHHL) — Documents needed
aliases: Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin toilet scheme
text: - A mobile number, to register and log in with an OTP for the online IHHL application.

title: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Overview
aliases: senior citizen saving scheme post office
text:
A government-backed 5-year savings deposit that pays interest every quarter. It is for people aged 60 or above, some retirees from age 55, and retired defence personnel from age 50. You can deposit from Rs 1,000 up to Rs 30 lakh at a post office or an authorised bank branch.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs (National Savings Institute); run through post offices and authorised banks.

title: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
aliases: senior citizen saving scheme post office
text:
- Aged 60 years or above on the day the account is opened.
- Aged 55 or more but below 60 and retired (on superannuation or otherwise): you can open the account only within 3 months of receiving your retirement benefits, and you cannot deposit more than the retirement benefits you received.
- Retired defence services personnel (not civilian defence employees) can open an account from age 50, if they meet the other conditions.
- The account can be in your name alone or joint with your spouse only. In a joint account only the first holder's age counts, and the whole deposit belongs to the first holder.
- You may hold more than one SCSS account, but the total deposit across all of them must not exceed Rs 30 lakh. A husband and wife who are each eligible can each deposit up to Rs 30 lakh.
Not eligible:
- NRIs are not allowed to invest in national small savings schemes such as SCSS.
- People below 55 cannot open an account, except retired defence personnel aged 50 or more, and the spouse of a government employee who died in service after reaching 50.
- People aged 55 to 59 who have not retired cannot open an account.

title: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
aliases: senior citizen saving scheme post office
text: - The legal heir of an employee who died while still in service cannot deposit that employee's terminal benefits in SCSS.

title: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Benefits
aliases: senior citizen saving scheme post office
text:
- Make one lump-sum deposit of at least Rs 1,000, in multiples of Rs 1,000, up to Rs 30 lakh.
- Interest is paid every quarter, on the first working day of April, July, October and January. It can be credited straight to your savings account.
- The deposit matures after 5 years. You can extend it for another 3 years by applying within 1 year of maturity.
- The deposit qualifies for an income tax deduction under Section 80C.
- You can close the account early. Before 1 year, any interest already paid is taken back. Between 1 and 2 years, 1.5% of the deposit is deducted. After 2 years, 1% is deducted. An extended account can be closed without deduction after 1 year of extension.
- If the account holder dies, the deposit with interest goes to the nominee or legal heirs. A spouse who is the joint holder or sole nominee, and who is eligible, can continue the account.

title: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — How to apply
aliases: senior citizen saving scheme post office
text:
- Open the account at any post office or at a bank branch designated for SCSS.
- Fill in the account opening form (Form-1) and make the deposit in one go.
- Interest rates are set by the Ministry of Finance every quarter, so ask the post office or bank for the rate in force on the day you deposit.

title: Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) — Documents needed
aliases: senior citizen saving scheme post office
text: - Retirees aged 55 to 60, and defence retirees from 50: proof of the date the retirement benefits were paid, and a certificate from the employer giving details of the retirement, the benefits, and the post and period of employment.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Overview
text:
A government small-savings account for a girl child, opened by her parent or guardian before she turns 10, at a post office or authorised bank. Yearly deposits from Rs 250 to Rs 1.5 lakh earn a government-set interest rate with tax benefits, and the account matures 21 years after opening.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs (National Savings Institute).

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Eligibility rules
text:
- The account is opened in the name of a girl child by her parent or guardian.
- The girl must be aged 9 or younger on the day the account is opened; it cannot be opened once she turns 10.
- Each girl can have only one account.
- A family can open accounts for at most 2 girls; more are allowed only when twins or triplets are born in the first or second birth, backed by an affidavit and birth certificates.
Not eligible:
- A girl who has already turned 10 cannot get a new account.
- A girl who already has an account cannot open a second one.
- A third girl in the same family cannot get an account unless the extra girls are twins or triplets from the first or second birth.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Benefits
text:
- You can deposit from Rs 250 up to Rs 1.5 lakh (Rs 1,50,000) in a financial year, in multiples of Rs 50; at least Rs 250 must be deposited each year.
- Deposits are made for 15 years from opening, and the account matures after 21 years.
- Interest is fixed by the government and changed from time to time; it was 8.2% a year from 1 January 2024 to 30 September 2026, added to the account once a year.
- Up to 50% of the balance (as at the end of the previous financial year) can be withdrawn for the girl's education once she turns 18 or passes Class 10, whichever is earlier.
- The account can be closed early for the girl's marriage after she turns 18, and on serious compassionate grounds (such as a life-threatening illness or the guardian's death) after 5 years.
- Deposits get income tax deduction under Section 80C and the interest earned is tax free.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — How to apply
text:
- Open the account at any post office or authorised bank branch by filling Form-1.
- The parent or guardian runs the account until the girl turns 18; after that she can operate it herself.
- If the minimum Rs 250 is missed in a year, the account can be revived within 15 years of opening by paying Rs 50 penalty for each missed year plus the missed minimum deposits.
- The account can be transferred to any post office or bank anywhere in India.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Documents needed
text:
- Birth certificate of the girl child.
- Identity and address (KYC) documents of the parent or guardian.
- For a third account due to twins or triplets: an affidavit from the guardian with the children's birth certificates.

title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Overview
text:
Every rural household whose adult members ask for unskilled manual work has a legal guarantee of at least 125 days of paid work in each financial year. The guarantee came into force on 1 July 2026 and replaced MGNREGA, which was repealed the same day.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.

title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Eligibility rules
text:
- The household lives in a rural area. The guarantee applies in all rural areas of India from 1 July 2026.
- Work is given to adult members, meaning people who have completed 18 years of age.
- Adult members must be willing to do unskilled manual work.
- The household needs a Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card. Existing MGNREGA job cards with completed e-KYC stay valid until the new cards are issued.
Not eligible:
- Households in urban areas are not covered; the Act applies only to rural areas.
- Persons below 18 years of age cannot be given work under the scheme.

title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Benefits (part 1 of 2)
text:
- At least 125 days of wage employment per household in every financial year, up from 100 days under MGNREGA.
- Work must be given within 15 days of applying. If it is not, the State must pay an unemployment allowance: at least one-fourth of the notified wage rate for the first 30 days in the year, and at least one-half for the rest of the year.
- Wages are paid weekly, and in any case within 15 days of the muster roll closing. They go straight into the worker's bank or post office account by DBT. If wages are late, the worker gets delay compensation of 0.05% of the unpaid wages for each day of delay.
- Work is given within 5 km of the applicant's village where possible. If it is farther away (but within the Block), an extra 10% of the wage rate is paid for travel and living costs.
- Worksites must have drinking water, shade and a first-aid kit. Injured workers get free treatment, and if hospitalised, a daily allowance of half the wage rate. If five or more children under five are present, a woman worker is paid to look after them.

title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Benefits (part 2 of 2)
text: - States may stop works for up to 60 days a year in peak sowing and harvesting seasons, but the full 125 days must still be given during the rest of the year.

title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — How to apply
text:
- To get a Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card, register the household at the Gram Panchayat. Any adult member gives the names, ages and address of the household members.
- Ask for work at the Gram Panchayat, with the Programme Officer or with any authorised person. You can ask orally, in writing on Form 6, or through digital platforms.
- You cannot be refused work only because your e-KYC is pending. e-KYC can be completed later, including at the worksite.

title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Documents needed
text:
- Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card (or an e-KYC-verified MGNREGA job card during the transition).
- Aadhaar, for e-KYC and face-authentication attendance at the worksite.
- Bank or post office account for wage payment.
